questions.question: NITI is abbreviation for_________.
questions.questionHtml: NITI is abbreviation for_________.
questions.solution: NITI stands for National Institution for Transforming India. It is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established in 2015, to achieve sustainable development goals and enhance cooperative federalism. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission, which used to formulate five-year plans for the country's development.

questions.question: What is the intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions called?
questions.questionHtml: What is the intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions called?
questions.solution: Panchayat Samiti operates at the block level, linking Gram Panchayats and Zilla Parishads. Established under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, it oversees local governance, law enforcement, and economic development in rural India, forming a crucial tier of the decentralized governance structure.

questions.question: Pipelines as a means of transport are looked after by the _______ of the Government of India.

options.text: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
options.html: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

options.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
options.html: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

questions.solution: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in India is responsible for the exploration, production, refining, distribution, marketing, import, export, and conservation of petroleum, natural gas, petroleum products, and liquefied natural gas. It oversees the planning, development, and implementation of policies to ensure efficient and sustainable use of these resources, including the development and maintenance of pipelines. The Ministry ensures supply security, promotes energy efficiency, reduces environmental impact, attracts investments, and collaborates internationally to secure energy resources and enhance global energy security.

questions.question: In the context of Elections in India, the term VVPAT stands for:
questions.questionHtml: In the context of Elections in India, the term VVPAT stands for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail.

Key Points

In the context of Elections in India, the term VVPAT stands for Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail.

  • VVPAT is the system that allows voters to verify their votes.
  • The VVPAT machine prints a slip along with the name of the candidate and the corresponding election symbol and automatically drops it in a sealed box.
  • It was first introduced in India in 2013.
  • VVPAT was first used in Noksen (assembly constituency) in Nagaland.
  • It can be accessed by polling officers only.
  • During the 2019 general election, VVPAT was introduced in all 543 Lok Sabha constituencies.

questions.question: In which year was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) established?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) established?
questions.solution: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established on 8th December 1985. The Charter was signed by the leaders of eight South Asian nations- Bangladesh, Bhutan, Afghanistan, Maldives, Nepal, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894?
questions.questionHtml: Who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894?
questions.solution: Baron Pierre de Coubertin founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894 to revive the ancient Olympic Games and promote global friendship through sports. The IOC is the highest authority of the Olympic movement and is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. The Olympic Games occur every four years, alternating between Summer and Winter Games every two years. The Olympic motto, "Citius, Altius, Fortius," means "Faster, Higher, Stronger," and the symbol of five interlocking rings represents the unity of the five continents. The Olympic Charter outlines the principles and rules of Olympism.

questions.question: Nitish Kumar, who took an oath as the Chief Minister of Bihar on 16 November 2020, belongs to which of the following parties?
questions.questionHtml: Nitish Kumar, who took an oath as the Chief Minister of Bihar on 16 November 2020, belongs to which of the following parties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Janata Dal United.

Important Points

  • Nitish Kumar, who took an oath as the Chief Minister of Bihar on 16 November 2020, belongs to Janata Dal United.
  • The Janata Party was a political party that was founded as an amalgam of Indian political parties opposed to the Emergency that was imposed between 1975 to 1977 by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi of the Indian National Congress.
  • In the 1977 general election, the party defeated the Congress and Janata leader Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress prime minister in independent modern India's history.
  • Nitish Kumar started his political career with Janata Party.
  • The rationale of the formation was that of preserving national security.
  • When the State of Emergency was lifted and new elections called in 1977, opposition political parties such as the Congress (O), Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Bharatiya Lok Dal as well as defectors from the Congress (R) joined to form the Janata Party, which won a sweeping majority in the Indian Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian political party system?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian political party system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Single party system

Key Points

  • India has a multi-party system, which means that multiple political parties can and do contest elections across the country.
  • A single party system is a system in which only one political party is legally allowed to hold power, which is not the case in India.
  • The presence of numerous political parties in India leads to the formation of coalition governments, especially at the central level.
  • The lack of effective opposition and factions and defections are also features seen within the Indian political party system due to the diverse and fragmented nature of the electorate.

Additional Information

  • The Indian political party system is characterized by a high level of political pluralism.
  • There are several national and regional parties that play significant roles in the political landscape of the country.
  • The Election Commission of India oversees the electoral process to ensure free and fair elections across the country.
  • The Indian Constitution provides for a democratic system of governance, ensuring the representation of diverse groups and interests.
  • Coalition politics is a common phenomenon in India due to the multi-party system, especially in forming governments at both the central and state levels.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the first elected Parliament come into existence?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years did the first elected Parliament come into existence?
questions.solution: In the year 1952, the first Elected Parliament with two houses came into being in India. The first general elections under the new Constitution were held during the year 1951-52. The first elected Parliament came into existence in April 1952.

questions.question: The UIDAI is under the jurisdiction of which of the following ministries?
questions.questionHtml: The UIDAI is under the jurisdiction of which of the following ministries?

options.text: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
options.html: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

questions.solution: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) falls under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. UIDAI is responsible for issuing Aadhaar cards, which are unique identification numbers assigned to Indian residents. This ministry is the most relevant because UIDAI's core function is related to digital identity and technology. While the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, and Ministry of Home Affairs intersect with UIDAI's operations in financial transactions, education, and security, respectively, their primary functions do not align directly with UIDAI's focus on technology and information management.

questions.question: Which body in India is responsible for safeguarding and promoting the rights of consumers and ensuring consumer protection?
questions.questionHtml: Which body in India is responsible for safeguarding and promoting the rights of consumers and ensuring consumer protection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC)Key Points

  •  In India, the Department of Consumer Affairs (DoCA) and the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) are responsible for consumer protection: 
  • Department of Consumer Affairs (DoCA)
    • A department under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, that implements consumer protection laws and regulations.
    • The DoCA also established the National Consumer Helpline portal called "Integrated Grievance Redressal Mechanism- INGRAM" for consumers to report complaints. 

Additional Information

  • Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)
    • A regulatory authority established under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 to: 
    • Protect, promote, and enforce consumer rights 
    • Prevent unfair trade practices 
    • Ensure that false or misleading advertisements are not made 
    • The CCPA works with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) to address issues that impact consumer safety and satisfaction.

questions.question: According to World Health Organization (WHO), “Hygiene refers to ______ and practices that help to maintain ______ and ______ the spread of diseases.”
questions.questionHtml: According to World Health Organization (WHO), “Hygiene refers to ______ and practices that help to maintain ______ and ______ the spread of diseases.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is conditions, health, prevent.

  • According to World Health Organization (WHO), “Hygiene refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.

Key Points

  • Hygiene refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.
  • Medical hygiene, therefore, includes a specific set of practices associated with this preservation of health, for example, environmental cleaning, sterilization of equipment, hand hygiene, water and sanitation and safe disposal of medical waste.
  • Personal hygiene refers to maintaining the body's cleanliness.

Additional Information

  • World Health Organization (WHO)
    • WHO is the United Nations agency that connects nations, partners and people to promote health, keep the world safe and serve the vulnerable – so everyone, everywhere can attain the highest level of health.
    • Working with 194 Member States across 6 regions and on the ground in 150+ locations, the WHO team works to improve everyone’s ability to enjoy good health and well-being.
    • India is a member of WHO.​
    • Establishment: April 7th, 1948
    • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations has declared October 2 as the International Day of Non-violence to honour Gandhi’s ways?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following organisations has declared October 2 as the International Day of Non-violence to honour Gandhi’s ways?

options.text: International Federation Red Cross and Red Crescent
options.html: International Federation Red Cross and Red Crescent

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is United National General Assembly.

Key Points

  • The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) declared October 2 as the International Day of Non-Violence.
  • This day commemorates the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, a global leader in the non-violence movement.
  • The day aims to disseminate the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.
  • It was established by the UNGA resolution A/RES/61/271 on June 15, 2007.
  • The resolution reaffirms the universal relevance of the principle of non-violence and the desire to secure a culture of peace, tolerance, understanding, and non-violence.

 Additional Information

  • International Federation Red Cross and Red Crescent
    • The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world's largest humanitarian network.
    • It provides assistance without discrimination as to nationality, race, religious beliefs, class, or political opinions.
    • Founded in 1919 in Paris in the aftermath of World War I.
  • United Nations Development Fund
    • The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) works in around 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion.
    • UNDP helps countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities, and build resilience to sustain development results.
  • Amnesty International
    • Amnesty International is a global movement of more than 7 million people who take injustice personally.
    • They are campaigning for a world where human rights are enjoyed by all.
    • Founded in 1961 by the lawyer Peter Benenson.

questions.question: The International Olympic Committee was established in the year ________.
questions.questionHtml: The International Olympic Committee was established in the year ________.
questions.solution: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was established in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin in Paris to revive the ancient Olympic Games. As the supreme authority of the Olympic Movement, the IOC oversees the organization of the Summer and Winter Olympic Games, held every four years. The IOC operates under the Olympic Charter, collaborating with National Olympic Committees (NOCs) worldwide to facilitate athlete participation. The ancient Olympic Games date back to 8th century BC in Greece. Additional governing bodies include the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the Asian Olympic Council (AOC). The Commonwealth and Asian Games are other significant multi-sport events.

questions.question: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission established in India?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission established in India?
questions.solution: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in India on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. Its primary goal is to safeguard and promote human rights, encompassing civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights as outlined by the Constitution and international treaties. The NHRC is composed of a chairperson (a retired Chief Justice of India), judiciary members, human rights experts, and representatives from minority and marginalized groups. It investigates human rights violations, recommends government actions, conducts awareness programs, and provides advice on human rights laws and policies.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations awards the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following organisations awards the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences?

options.text: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
options.html: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

Key Points

  • The Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, officially the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is a prize awarded by the Nobel Foundation for Economic Sciences.
  • The Prize in Economic Sciences is associated with the Nobel Prize, despite the fact that it was not established by Alfred Nobel's will in 1895.
  • Its winners are announced alongside the Nobel Prize honorees, and it is delivered at the Nobel Prize Award Ceremony.
  • As a result, it is also known as the Nobel Prize in Economics. The Nobel Prize was founded in 1968 by a gift to the Nobel Foundation by Sweden's central bank, Sveriges Riksbank, to honour the bank's 300th anniversary.

Important Points

  • The Nobel Foundation administers and refers to it, along with the Nobel Prizes.
  • The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences chooses the Laureates for the Memorial Prize in Economics.
  • The prize was initially given to Dutch economist Jan Tinbergen and Norwegian economist Ragnar Frisch in 1969 for "developing and applying dynamic models for the investigation of economic processes."

questions.question: Which of the following ministries has the responsibility of organising the Republic Day parade in Delhi?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following ministries has the responsibility of organising the Republic Day parade in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ministry of Defence.

Key Points

  • The Republic Day Parade is organised by the Ministry of Defence.
  • The Republic Day Parade held in Delhi showcases the country's military might, cultural diversity and tableaux from various states.
  • The Ministry of Defence is responsible for organising and coordinating the parade, in which the Indian Army, Air Force and Navy play a major role.

  • Foreign dignitaries are invited as chief guests at the Republic Day Parade.

Additional Information

  • Republic Day:
    • The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.
    • This day marks India becoming a full-fledged republic.
    • The Republic Day parade showcases the country's military might and cultural heritage.
  • Rajpath renamed as Kartavya Path​:
    • In September 2022, Rajpath was renamed as Kartavya Path.
    • Its purpose was to depict it as a symbol of service to the public and performance of duty.
  • Chief Guest​:
    • Every year a foreign leader is invited as the chief guest at the Republic Day parade.
    • This is a symbolic move to strengthen India's bilateral relations and diplomacy.
  • Parade tableaux:
    • The parade showcases tableaux from various states and union territories, showcasing their cultural and historical heritage.
    • The tableaux are approved and coordinated by the Ministry of Defence.

questions.question: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) which adopted 'Agenda 21' was held at:
questions.questionHtml: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) which adopted 'Agenda 21' was held at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rio de Janeiro.

Key Points

  • Agenda 21: ​
    • Agenda 21 is an action plan of the United Nations (UN) related to sustainable development and was an outcome of the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in 1992.
    • It is a comprehensive blueprint of action to be taken globally, nationally, and locally by organizations of the UN, governments, and major groups in every area in which humans directly affect the environment. The number 21 refers to an agenda for the 21st century.

Important Points 

  • Local Agenda 21: 
    • ​​The implementation of Agenda 21 was intended to involve action at international, national, regional, and local levels.
    • Some national and state governments have legislated or advised that local authorities take steps to implement the plan locally, as recommended in Chapter 28 of the document. Such programs are often known as ‘Local Agenda 21.
  • Agenda 21 for culture:
    • During the first World Public Meeting on Culture, held in Porto Alegre, Brazil in 2002, it came up with the idea to draw up document guidelines for local cultural policies, a document comparable to what Agenda 21 meant in 1992 for the environment.
    • Agenda 21 for culture is the first document with a worldwide mission that advocates establishing the groundwork of an undertaking by cities and local governments for cultural development.

Additional Information

  • There are 40 chapters in Agenda 21, divided into four main sections.
  • It is grouped into 4 sections:-
    • Section I - Social and Economic Dimensions
    • Section II - Conservation and Management of Resources for Development
    • Section III - Strengthening the Role of Major Groups
    • Section IV - Means of Implementation

questions.question: In which of the following states/union territories was an election NOT held during March-April 2021?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following states/union territories was an election NOT held during March-April 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bihar.

Key Points

  • The election was NOT held in Bihar during March-April 2021.
  • Members of the Seventeenth Bihar Legislative Assembly were elected in three parts from October to November.
  • The previous Bihar Sixteenth Legislative Assembly's tenure concluded on November 29, 2020.
  • Following the elections, incumbent Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was re-sworn in as Chief Minister after being chosen as the leader of the National Democratic Alliance in Bihar, and two new deputy Chief Ministers, Tarkishore Prasad, and Renu Devi were recruited into the new administration.

Important Points

  • The election for 292 of the 294 constituencies of West Bengal's Legislative Assembly in 2021 was held in eight phases between March 27 and April 29, 2021.
  • The election for the remaining two seats had been postponed until September 30, 2021.
  • Despite opinion surveys generally expecting a close fight against the Bharatiya Janata Party, which formed the formal opposition with 77 seats, the incumbent All India Trinamool Congress administration led by Mamata Banerjee won the election by a substantial margin.
  • On April 6, 2021, the Sixteenth Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Election was conducted to elect representatives from the state's 234 constituencies. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) won the election, ending the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam's decade-long reign (AIADMK).
  • M. K. Stalin, the leader of the DMK, was elected as the eighth Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, and the 12th since the 1956 reorganization. He took the place of AIADMK leader Edappadi K. Palaniswami.
  • The fifteenth legislative assembly election was held on April 6, 2021, in the union territory of Puducherry, India, to elect members to the Legislative Assembly from 30 constituencies.

questions.question: In which year was the Communist Party of India - Marxist (CPI-M) formed?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the Communist Party of India - Marxist (CPI-M) formed?
questions.solution: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) was formed in 1964. It emerged after splitting from the Communist Party of India during the Seventh Congress in Calcutta. CPI(M) is a prominent party, especially in Kerala, with its headquarters in New Delhi.
